summary: Scheduled report attachment contains tracehook links that resolve to previous org/context after retention prune
summary_detail: Daily scheduled PDF report (org-scoped) included dashboard links with tracehook tokens that, after retention prune/compact job, started resolving to a different org context (previous tenant) or 404. Multiple customer recipients reported stale trace context and broken drilldowns.
description:
Issue summary:
Customer ClearHealth Analytics reports that scheduled daily PDF reports sent at 02:15 UTC contain embedded dashboard links with tracehook parameters. After our retention compaction/eviction job ran on 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC, recipients who opened the links saw either 404 or the dashboard loaded into a different org-scoped context (old org id) resulting in missing metrics and broken drilldowns.

Impact:
- Customer-facing scheduled reports (PDF+link) show stale or wrong tracehook context for ~70% of recipients for the 2026-03-12 and 2026-03-13 deliveries.
- Several business teams rely on the drilldown links for operational alerts; this caused confusion and delayed incident response.
- Reported by customer success; no token-level billing impact observed.

Observed behavior vs expected:
- Observed: Embedded links include a tracehook param (th=...) whose signature or namespace resolves to a previous org id or returns 404 after retention prune runs.
- Expected: Links should resolve to the correct org context and persist across retention compaction/backfill events for scheduled report deliveries until the link TTL/expiration is hit.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a dashboard with a tracehook-enabled drilldown (org-scoped) in prod us-east.
2) Schedule daily PDF+links report to be sent at 02:15 UTC to an external recipient list for org X.
3) Allow retention compaction/eviction to run on midnight/02:00 UTC window (we ran the compact job on 2026-03-12 02:00).
4) Open the delivered PDF and click the embedded tracehook link after the compact job completes.
5) Observe link resolves to wrong org context or 404 (trace context missing or key namespace rotated).
logs: 2026-03-12T02:00:12Z compact-worker-7 INFO retention: started compaction for tenant-metadata-shard orgs 1024..2047
2026-03-12T02:00:34Z link-service-3 WARN tracehook: signature-rotate triggered for org 0x1a2b; new namespace assigned 0x1a2b:v2
2026-03-12T02:15:03Z scheduler-4 INFO reports: generated PDF report id=rep-33892 recipients=23 attachments=pdf,links
2026-03-12T02:15:05Z link-service-3 DEBUG link-gen: produced link https://console.redwood.ai/dash/zz?th=eyJvcmciOjEwMiwi... expired=false namespace=0x1a2b
2026-03-12T02:16:10Z nginx-proxy-1 ERROR 404 GET /d/zz (tracehook signature mismatch) from 18.204.12.7
investigation_notes: Initial triage by CS showed customer opened 12 separate recipient links; 8 failed with 404 and 4 loaded with an unrelated org context (org id 0x1a2b-old).
Hypothesis A: retention prune triggered a short-lived namespace rotation for tracehook signing keys; scheduled reports generated before rotation used old namespace that the router no longer accepts.
Hypothesis B: link encoding includes a tenant mapping that is looked up lazily at click-time; compaction removed the mapping entry and defaulted to previously cached org mapping (race).

Checked artifacts: tracehook key rotation log lines present at 02:00:34Z coincident with compact job. Link generation happened at 02:15:05Z (after rotation) but signatures appear to carry legacy namespace sometimes (race in background job that re-signed some pending links).
Repro on staging: reproduced when running compactor concurrently with a scheduled-report generator; observed link namespace header mismatch if link-gen worker picked an in-flight key object.
customer_reported_samples: Recipient A (external): clicked link -> 404; HTTP response body contains 'tracehook signature invalid or missing'.
Recipient B (internal): clicked link -> dashboard loads but top-left shows org label 'ClearHealth-OLD' and metric panels empty.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer reported 12 recipients impacted. Asked for immediate mitigation to stop further deliveries until fix.

Darin Chen (SRE) 2026-03-12: Added to SRE queue. Initial repro on staging: compactor and report-generator race causes inconsistent namespace resolution. Possible quick mitigation: pause scheduled report sends for affected orgs while we patch link-generator to read a stable key snapshot.
Marco Ruiz (Backend) 2026-03-13: Patch ready to ensure report generator pins keyset snapshot at job start. Will deploy to canary today. Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/link-service/pull/2387
Sabrina Lee (CS) 2026-03-13: Customer accepted workaround: re-run the 2026-03-12 report and send regenerated attachments; they will confirm once recipients verify links.
Darin Chen (SRE) 2026-03-14: Canary passed; rolling full deployment to prod schedule-link-gen cluster. Monitoring for 24h for regressions.
workaround: Customer success re-generated and resent the affected daily report for 2026-03-12 with freshly signed links. Short-term: CS paused the daily schedule for ClearHealth until patch rolled out.
resolution: Deployed patch to report link-generator to pin a stable tracehook keyset snapshot at job start, preventing races with retention/compaction rotation. Added a post-deploy check in the scheduler: verify link signatures against active keyset before enqueueing emails. Scheduled a follow-up runbook change to avoid compaction during scheduled-report windows for enterprise tier orgs. Pending: customer confirmation of successful regenerated report deliveries (expected by 2026-03-15).
follow_up_actions: 1) Update runbook: avoid key rotation/compaction windows overlapping with scheduled-report times for orgs with active scheduled deliveries.
2) Add end-to-end alert that verifies a sample of scheduled-report links resolve within 5 minutes of send.
3) Postmortem to be drafted in Confluence (owner: Darin Chen) within 72 hours.
4) Consider increasing TTL for link metadata mapping used by scheduled-report generator for enterprise tier customers.
